head: 47 crossings.
15 with
a test.
body: I would have told you, confidently, that it was fine.
I had been quoting the migration count as a strength.

head: The boat only
*rows one way
slides.caption: A migration is the only code you ship that gets exactly one attempt, on a device you cannot see, against data you cannot reproduce.

head: Everything else
gets a
second chance
body: A bad screen gets a hotfix. A failed request gets retried. A crash gets a patch release.
If a migration is wrong the data is not broken, it is gone, and the row you would recover from is the one that did not survive.

items.title: Foreign key changes
items.sub: SQLite recreates the table and copies every row

items.title: Data moves
items.sub: INSERT INTO ... SELECT transforms content, loses nothing

head: Assert the data,
not the schema
callout: Reading a row back is the only thing that proves anything survived the crossing.

head: Pay the toll
before you get
*on the boat
body: I did not find a bug this week. I found thirty-five crossings I had never rehearsed, and four of them touch the things that actually eat data.
47 migrations sounds like maturity. It is only maturity if you can say what happens when each one runs.
